attribution.note: Marcus's own post restating his earlier position in his own words and endorsing it.

semantics.note: 'Never be able to trust' is firm, unhedged language about a lasting outcome. Treating it as an endorsed, ongoing forecast with no deadline is faithful to the words.

contract.note: The plain reading (practical reliance without routine checking, not perfection) is an ordinary one that leans neither for nor against Marcus. 'Never' has no deadline, so only a conclusive demonstration or an impossibility result could settle it early.

evidence.note: Peer-reviewed paper (April 2026) finds hallucinations persist in top models and proposes fixes. It shows neither permanent impossibility nor a breakthrough.
Preprint posted before the cutoff: one model had zero hallucinations on 70 prompts but poor recall. That is a narrow result, not broad practical reliability.
Measurements from October 2026 (the publisher sells a verification product): every model invented some sources on hard questions. This shows a current, bounded problem, not a permanent limit.

reviews.rationale: This is an endorsed forecast with no deadline. The evidence shows errors continuing and one narrow zero-hallucination result. Neither meets the contract's rule for early resolution: no conclusive impossibility result and no independently replicated demonstration of broad reliability. The forecast stays unresolved.
